Luke 1:1

Reviewed units still unfinished

  • Luke 1:21: The waiting congregation's wonder was reread with Zechariah's actual emergence. The previously considered Moses-delay scene has a different action and response; generic delay does not add a specific useful comparison to this sanctuary waiting.
  • Luke 1:23: Completion of service and return home were reread with the previously considered priestly-division background. No exact shift date, Jehoiada incident identity or same departure action is established for Zechariah.
  • Luke 2:44: The mistaken company assumption and search among relatives/acquaintances remain the narrated facts. The later temple discovery does not add a separate family-search counterpart, and no moral allegory about being lost is supplied.
  • Luke 2:45: The return to Jerusalem and continued search were reconsidered with the following finding. This remains the local search sequence, without a further particular return-and-search comparison or an invented journey total.
  • Luke 3:24: The Matthat–Levi–Melchi–Jannai–Joseph sequence remains unestablished by a matching lineage. Familiar repeated names are not merged with other people.
  • Luke 3:25: The Mattathias–Amos–Nahum–Esli–Naggai sequence was reread as ancestry. Its names are not identified with prophetic authors or a different genealogy through spelling alone.
  • Luke 3:26: The Maath–Mattathias–Semein–Josech–Joda chain remains the preserved chain. No separate supported sequence or biographical identity has been established.
  • Luke 3:28: The Melchi–Addi–Cosam–Elmadam–Er chain remains distinct from isolated people bearing related names. No missing genealogical links are supplied.
